format: Pokemon Champions VGC Reg M-C doubles (bring 6, pick 4, one Mega per battle, species clause) inside Anthony's 10-pick / 100-point draft league
readme: Spec for the 'Cores to fear' feature. cores.md explains the reasoning. raw/cores-check.py is a reference implementation of every rule here and prints the league results and test cases quoted in cores.md.

dataModel.source: data/dex.json -> species[id]: num, roles[], keyMoves[], forms[] {name, types[], abilities[], baseStats{hp,atk,def,spa,spd,spe}, mega?: true}. typechart[attackType][defendType] = multiplier.
dataModel.option: An OPTION is one (species, form, ability) triple: the form a mon is in when it does the job, plus the one ability it has. A base form with 3 listed abilities yields 3 options. A Mega form has 1 ability. Moves belong to the species: Megas share the base learnset.

evidence.usage: The move is in species.keyMoves (Pikalytics top moves for Reg M-C, snapshot 2026-10-02). This means it's commonly run. It doesn't mean this coach runs it.
evidence.learnset: The move is only known to be learnable: the species has the role tag in moveTags, or the move is in learnsetTech[]. It's a set choice the coach may or may not make.
evidence.learnsetTechNote: dex.json has no full learnsets. Only role tags cover move groups. For single tech moves that no tag covers (Imprison, Taunt, Brick Break, Psychic Fangs, Defog, Ally Switch, Mean Look, Block, Soundproof is an ability), add species.learnsetTech[] in tools/build-data.mjs from docs/research/strategy/raw/champions-learnsets-board.json, limited to the move ids in techMoves below. Until then those moves can only match through keyMoves.

dataModel.moveTagCaveat: A group tag (screens, redirection, speed-drop, pivot) says the species learns at least one move of the group, not which one. A tag match is evidence 'learnset' for the group and never 'usage'.

conditionLanguage.move: {kind:'move', value: name | [names]}: matches every option of the species (Megas keep the moveset). evidence = 'usage' if any value is in keyMoves, else 'learnset' if a value's moveTags tag is in roles or the value is in learnsetTech[], else no match.
conditionLanguage.ability: {kind:'ability', value:[names]}: matches an option whose ability is in the list.
conditionLanguage.type: {kind:'type', value:[types]}: matches an option whose form has any listed type.
conditionLanguage.stats: {kind:'stats', spe?:{'<=':n}|{'>=':n}, atkOrSpa?:{'>=':n}, spa?:{'>=':n}, spaOverAtk?:true}: compares the option form's baseStats. atkOrSpa = max(atk, spa).
conditionLanguage.defense: {kind:'defense', attackType:T, maxMult:m}: the product of typechart[T][t] over the option form's types is <= m. Use 0 for immunity and 0.5 for 'resists or immune'.
conditionLanguage.stab: {kind:'stab', type:T, minStat:n}: the option form has type T and max(atk, spa) >= n. This is a coarse 'can hit hard with T'. It isn't a damage calc.
conditionLanguage.allOf: {allOf:[conds]}: one option must satisfy every listed condition. Move conditions are species-wide, so they combine with any option.
conditionLanguage.evidenceOfAllOf: The weakest evidence among the parts ('learnset' < 'usage'). Abilities, types and stats count as 'usage'.
conditionLanguage.minEvidence: Optional on any condition: {..., minEvidence:'usage'} rejects learnset-only matches. Used where learnset noise is high: Sunny Day / Rain Dance (most mons learn them), Reflect / Light Screen, Aurora Veil, Blizzard.

fieldability.scope: A core must fit inside the 4 Pokemon brought to one game (bring 6, pick 4). maxMembers = 4. It doesn't need all its members on the field at the same time.
algorithm: 1. For each roster mon, list its options. Drop the options that match no slot. Each mon becomes a list of (option, set of slots it satisfies, evidence, isMega).

2. Search over assignments: choose a subset S of roster mons with minDistinct <= |S| <= maxMembers. Give each mon in S EXACTLY ONE option. One option per mon means Charizard is base, Mega X or Mega Y, never two of them.
3. Require distinct species.num within S (species clause; one Rotom form).

4. Require at most ONE member whose chosen option is a Mega form (one Mega per battle). A role that exists only on a Mega form, e.g. Charizard-Mega-Y's Drought or Raichu-Mega-X's Electric Surge, uses up that one Mega.
5. For every slot, at least slot.min members of S must have a chosen option that satisfies the slot. A member may fill several slots: Salamence can be both the Tailwind setter and an attacker.

6. State: 'fieldable' if a legal assignment exists. 'mega-conflict' if none exists but one would exist when rule 4 is dropped. Otherwise not shown (the UI's 'forming' state is computed separately by adding one hypothetical member).
7. Among the legal assignments, report the best one: fewest Mega members, then the strongest evidence (all 'usage' beats any 'learnset'), then the fewest members, then the roster order.

8. confidence = 'likely' if the reported assignment uses only usage evidence, else 'possible'. In v1 the UI shows 'possible' cores folded or not at all, because many role tags are learnset-only (Metagross learns screens, nobody runs them).
fieldability.complexity: With pruning, each roster has 10 mons, at most about 4 surviving options each, and subsets of 4 or fewer, so brute force stays tiny.
fieldability.answersLegality: Anthony's side uses the same option model. An answer that needs a Mega form (e.g. Charizard-Mega-X's Fire/Dragon resistances) is megaDependent. When counting answers for status, at most ONE megaDependent mon counts, and non-Mega answers are preferred.
fieldability.slotPool: Besides the best assignment, report slotPool: for each slot, every roster mon that can fill it (any legal option, with evidence). The minimal assignment answers 'can they field it?'. The pool shows 'with what?'.

A.name: Pool-only knowledge (baseline)
A.known: Both coaches' drafted 10 (VERIFIED: the league's Drafts tab is a published Google Sheet that the app reads).
A.hidden: Which 6 are built, which 4 are brought, the Mega choice, moves, items, abilities, Stat Point spreads, leads.
A.assumptions: ASSUMPTION: you know your opponent far enough ahead to prep (not confirmed for this league). Bo1 vs Bo3 is UNVERIFIED.

B.name: Open team sheets at the match
B.known: Everything in A, plus the opponent's 6 with moves, items, abilities and Mega stone at team preview (TPCi-style OTS). VERIFIED only for TPCi events and as a Showdown option. ASSUMPTION for this league.
B.hidden: Which 4 are brought, leads, Mega timing, Stat Point spreads (TPCi OTS don't list stat investment; ASSUMPTION that a league sheet wouldn't either).
B.note: OTS shown at the match don't change the week's build. Only the pool is known when you build, as in A. OTS change team preview and play: a tech move is visible before the game, so it works as a deterrent the opponent can route around (don't bring the core) rather than as a trap.

prepScenarios.Bo3: If matches are Bo3, game 1 gives partial information only: the moves, items and abilities actually used, the Mega chosen that game and the 4 brought. Unused moves, items not revealed, the 2 benched mons and the other Mega option stay hidden. Games 2-3 sit between A and B. They are not equivalent to open team sheets.

structural.A: Full. It doesn't depend on hidden information.

standard-move.A: Full, but the opponent can predict it from usage and plan around it (e.g. Armor Tail vs Fake Out).
standard-move.B: Full. Now confirmed, so they will plan around it.

tech.A: High. Hidden until used, so the opponent has to guess whether you run it. Costs a move slot (or a team slot) that's weaker in other matchups.
tech.B: Medium. Visible at preview, so it works as a deterrent (they may not bring the core) more than as a trap.

answerValueByScenario.surpriseOwn: Same logic for Anthony's own plans. Under A, Charizard's Mega X vs Mega Y choice, Sinistcha Imprison and which 6 he builds stay hidden. Under B the Mega stone and moves are visible at preview.

statusRule.wording: Answers are 'candidate answers': the model checks typing, ability, base Speed and moves, not damage, coverage, items, partners or positioning.

answerClass.structural: Comes from type, ability or base Speed (kinds type/defense/ability/stats/stab). Doesn't rely on a specific move.
answerClass.standard-move: A move answer where the move is in the answering mon's keyMoves. The mon usually runs it, so no matchup-specific choice is needed. It can still be blocked (Taunt, Imprison, Fake Out, Wide Guard).
answerClass.tech: A move answer known only from the learnset. It's a set or team choice for this match. conditional = true, and the UI says 'if you run X'.

statusRule.count: One count per distinct Anthony mon (a mon with several answers counts once, at its best class: structural > standard-move > tech). counts:false entries are never counted. partial:true answers count toward the mon total but never meet the 'anchor' requirement. At most one megaDependent mon counts.
statusRule.anchor: An anchor is a counted answer of class structural or standard-move with partial false. In scenario columns where the core's prepSensitivity is High, tech answers are also anchors.
statusRule.rule: Has answers: >= 2 counted mons and >= 1 anchor. Thin: >= 1 counted mon but not Has answers. No answer found: 0 counted mons.
statusRule.whyAmendedFromUx: Same thresholds as the UX proposal, with two changes. (1) A standard-move answer (e.g. Sinistcha's own Trick Room, which it almost always runs) anchors like a structural one, because it doesn't depend on choosing tech for this match. It still shows in its own lane as 'usually runs X'. (2) partial answers (Intimidate vs a mixed core, Icy Wind vs Tailwind) never anchor.
statusRule.contested: A contested answer (see answerBlockers) counts toward the mon total but is never an anchor.
statusRule.redundancy: Also report, for each 'Has answers' card, whether it stays 'Has answers' when any single one of Anthony's answering mons is removed (KO'd, benched or Fake Out'd). If not, name that mon as the single point of failure.
statusRule.megaConflictCards: Strategy agrees with UX v2: a mega-conflict card is not 'fieldable' and sorts after fieldable cards with the 'Needs 2 Megas' chip. No separate status cap is needed, because the core can't be run as listed.
statusRule.answerFields: robust = structural kind (type/defense/ability/stats/stab). conditional = move-based: the UI says 'usually runs X' when the move is in that mon's keyMoves (class standard-move), else 'if you run X' (class tech). class is computed per answering mon, not stored.

cores.name: Trick Room + slow hitters
cores.oneLineWhy: Reverses speed order for 5 turns (the setting turn is one of them). Champions has no Choice Band or Specs and no Assault Vest, so bulky slow hitters stay strong.

answers.label: Own Trick Room
answers.note: Setting your own Trick Room while theirs is up ends it. You need the setter alive and able to move.
answers.failsTo: Fake Out or Taunt on your setter. Their Imprison.

answers.label: Imprison + Trick Room
answers.note: Imprison (priority 0) goes before Trick Room (-7) and stops foes using any move the user knows, Trick Room included.
answers.failsTo: Taunt on your Imprison user first. They can also leave Trick Room at home once they see Imprison is possible.

answers.label: Taunt the setter
answers.note: Taunt (priority 0) lands before Trick Room (priority -7) if the setter hasn't already been Taunt-proofed.
answers.failsTo: Mental Herb (in the M-C item pool), Oblivious or Aroma Veil, Good as Gold, Magic Bounce (Taunt is reflectable), a Dark-type setter or Armor Tail / Psychic Terrain if your Taunt is Prankster-boosted, redirection (Follow Me / Rage Powder).

answers.label: Fake Out the setter
answers.note: Buys one turn on the first turn the user is on the field.
answers.failsTo: Armor Tail (Farigiraf), Psychic Terrain on a grounded setter, Inner Focus, Ghost-type setters (Sinistcha), redirection. Champions makes Fake Out unselectable after the user's first action.

answers.label: Slow hitter of your own
answers.note: Their Trick Room also speeds up your slow hitter, so the board doesn't fully flip against you.
answers.failsTo: Their slower abusers still move first (Torkoal base 20).

answers.label: Tailwind doesn't help
answers.note: Under Trick Room, Tailwind makes your mons move later.

prepReasoning.A: The setter is visible in the pool, but whether they bring Trick Room, and their Mental Herb / Armor Tail / redirection protection, isn't. Most counters (Taunt, Imprison) are themselves tech you have to commit to in your 6.
prepReasoning.B: You see Mental Herb, Imprison and Taunt at preview, and so do they. The core still functions. Visibility mostly shifts who leads what.

cores.counterplayToAnswers: Armor Tail blocks priority (Fake Out, Prankster Taunt) aimed at its side [VERIFIED: Showdown abilities.ts]. Psychic Terrain blocks priority against grounded targets [VERIFIED: Showdown moves.ts]. Redirection pulls single-target Taunt and Fake Out.

cores.name: Tailwind + strong attackers
cores.oneLineWhy: Doubles their side's Speed for 4 turns including the setting turn. Base-100 Megas then outspeed every non-Tailwind mon in the format.

answers.label: Trick Room flips it
answers.note: Under Trick Room, doubled Speed makes them move last.
answers.failsTo: Prankster Taunt (Whimsicott), Fake Out on the setter, KOs on the slow setter before it moves.

answers.label: Own Tailwind
answers.note: Mirror Tailwind returns the game to base Speed comparisons.
answers.failsTo: Losing the setter first. Their faster base Speed in the mirror.

answers.label: Icy Wind / Electroweb
answers.note: -1 Speed on both foes. Doesn't undo a doubling alone.
answers.failsTo: Clear Body, Defiant / Competitive (they gain stats), Wide Guard, Protect.

answers.label: Priority attacks
answers.note: Moves before Speed order, but usually for low damage.
answers.failsTo: Psychic Terrain (grounded targets), Armor Tail, Quick Guard.

answers.label: Fake Out the setter
answers.note: Stops a non-Prankster setter for a turn.
answers.failsTo: Ghost-type or Inner Focus setters, Psychic Terrain / Armor Tail / redirection protecting the setter. Fake Out (+3) does go before Prankster Tailwind (+1).

answers.label: Taunt the setter
answers.note: Works on non-Prankster setters that move after your Taunt.
answers.failsTo: Prankster Tailwind is +1 and Taunt is 0, so Whimsicott sets first. Mental Herb. Magic Bounce.

answers.label: Intimidate
answers.note: Softens physical Tailwind attackers.
answers.failsTo: Special attackers, Defiant / Competitive / Inner Focus / Clear Body / Mirror Armor.

prepReasoning.A: Every competitive roster has speed control. Knowing it's coming lets you Protect or switch for 4 turns, but that costs your tempo too.
prepReasoning.B: Same. Seeing a Focus Sash on the setter or Prankster tells you whether Fake Out or Taunt will work.

cores.name: Sun + abusers
cores.oneLineWhy: Sun boosts Fire 1.5x and halves Water. Mega Charizard-Y (159 SpA) and Torkoal's Eruption are the payoff, with Chlorophyll users as speed.

answers.label: Own weather setter
answers.note: The last weather to start wins. A Mega's weather starts when it Mega Evolves (before moves), so it beats a lead setter on turn 1.
answers.failsTo: Their switching or re-Mega timing. Losing the setter. Your own weather-dependent mons if you swap weathers.

answers.label: Resists Fire
answers.note: Takes sun-boosted Fire for half or less.
answers.failsTo: Coverage (Solar Beam into Water/Rock, Ancient Power, Earth Power), spread damage on the partner.

answers.label: Flash Fire / Heatproof
answers.note: Blocks or halves Fire damage.
answers.failsTo: Non-Fire coverage. Heatproof is an alternative ability: Sinistcha with Heatproof gives up Hospitality.

answers.label: Wide Guard vs Heat Wave
answers.note: Blocks spread Heat Wave and Eruption for one turn.
answers.failsTo: Single-target Weather Ball / Solar Beam. Taunt.

answers.label: Rock or Water attacker
answers.note: Rock hits Charizard 4x. Water is halved in sun, so only Rock is listed.
answers.failsTo: Intimidate, Protect, Wide Guard on Rock Slide.

prepReasoning.A: The setter is public and the mechanic needs no surprise. Your answer is roster structure (an override or resists), which you'd bring anyway.
prepReasoning.B: Same. Preview shows the Mega stone, which tells you whether sun comes from Charizard-Y.

cores.name: Rain + abusers
cores.oneLineWhy: Rain gives 1.5x Water, Swift Swim doubling, 100% Thunder/Hurricane and a one-turn Electro Shot, and it shuts off opposing sun.

answers.label: Own weather setter
answers.note: Replaces rain. Last to start wins.
answers.failsTo: Re-entry of their setter. Prankster Rain Dance (Sableye, Klefki) re-sets it.

answers.label: Resists Water
answers.note: Takes boosted Water for half or less.
answers.failsTo: Electric / Hurricane / Ice coverage.

answers.label: Absorbs Water or Electric
answers.note: Immune to (and redirects, for Storm Drain / Lightning Rod) rain's main attacks.
answers.failsTo: Mold Breaker (Basculegion-F can have it), spread moves aren't redirected.

answers.label: Ground: Electric-immune
answers.note: Shrugs off Thunder and Electro Shot.
answers.failsTo: Water is super-effective on most Ground types.

cores.name: Sand + abusers
cores.oneLineWhy: Sand Rush doubles Speed, Rock-types get 1.5x SpD, and it overrides sun/rain. Mega Tyranitar keeps Sand Stream.

answers.label: Own weather setter
answers.note: Turns off Sand Rush.
answers.failsTo: Tyranitar re-entering. Mega timing.

answers.label: Resists Rock
answers.note: Blunts Rock Slide spam.
answers.failsTo: Earthquake / Iron Head coverage.

answers.label: Strong Water / Fighting hitter
answers.note: Super-effective on Tyranitar and Excadrill.
answers.failsTo: Doesn't stop the speed advantage.

answers.label: Trick Room
answers.note: Turns Sand Rush into a liability.
answers.failsTo: Same as any Trick Room: Taunt, Fake Out, KO on the setter.

answers.label: Wide Guard
answers.note: Blocks Rock Slide and Earthquake for a turn.
answers.failsTo: Single-target moves, Taunt.

prepReasoning.A: Mechanical. Prep changes your leads, not whether sand works.

cores.name: Snow + Aurora Veil
cores.oneLineWhy: Snow Warning enables Aurora Veil (cuts physical and special damage, about 0.67x in doubles), 100% Blizzard and +50% Def for Ice-types. Veil is the real payoff.

detection.note: minDistinct 1: Alolan Ninetales sets snow and Veil alone. That's still a plan worth a card.

answers.label: Own weather setter
answers.note: No snow means no new Veil.
answers.failsTo: A Veil that's already up stays for its 5 turns.

answers.label: Screen breaker
answers.note: Removes Veil/screens from their side.
answers.failsTo: Ghost-types block Brick Break / Raging Bull (Normal form) damage. Protect.

answers.label: Infiltrator
answers.note: Ignores screens and Veil.
answers.failsTo: Nothing specific to Veil.

answers.label: Strong Fire / Steel hitter
answers.note: Super-effective into Ice-types.
answers.failsTo: Veil cuts it to about 0.67x in doubles.

answers.label: Taunt the setter
answers.note: Prevents Veil if it lands first.
answers.failsTo: A faster setter. Mental Herb. Focus Sash setters still get it up the next turn.

prepReasoning.A: Veil's value is front-loaded and the setter is public. A screen breaker or weather override in your 6 cuts most of it.
prepReasoning.B: Preview confirms Veil and Light Clay. Same answers.

cores.name: Psychic Terrain spam
cores.oneLineWhy: Psychic Surge blocks all priority (Fake Out, Prankster, Sucker Punch) aimed at grounded mons and turns Expanding Force into a boosted spread move.

answers.label: Dark-type: Psychic-immune
answers.note: Immune to Expanding Force.
answers.failsTo: Fighting / Bug / Fairy coverage. Psychic Terrain still blocks its priority.

answers.label: Resists Psychic
answers.note: Steel / Psychic halve it.
answers.failsTo: Fire coverage (Armarouge) into Steel.

answers.label: Own terrain setter
answers.note: Replaces Psychic Terrain on entry.
answers.failsTo: Their setter switching back in.

answers.label: Wide Guard
answers.note: Blocks terrain-boosted spread Expanding Force.
answers.failsTo: Single-target Psychic moves.

answers.label: Fake Out doesn't work here
answers.note: Psychic Terrain blocks priority against grounded targets, so Fake Out and Prankster moves fail.

prepReasoning.A: A Dark-type or a second terrain is easy to bring once you've seen Indeedee in the pool. The core still functions; you're cutting its damage, not stopping it.
prepReasoning.B: Same, plus preview shows whether Indeedee is built for Trick Room or for spam.

cores.name: Electric Terrain offense
cores.oneLineWhy: Electric Surge (Raichu-Mega-X, Pincurchin) gives 1.3x Electric to grounded attackers and stops sleep.

answers.label: Ground: Electric-immune
answers.note: Immune to every Electric move.
answers.failsTo: Grass / Water / Ice coverage (Raichu-Y's Focus Blast is Fighting).

answers.label: Lightning Rod / Volt Absorb
answers.note: Absorbs Electric. Lightning Rod also redirects it.
answers.failsTo: Spread Discharge isn't redirected. Mold Breaker.

answers.label: Resists Electric
answers.note: Grass / Electric / Dragon halve it.
answers.failsTo: Coverage.

answers.label: Own terrain setter
answers.note: Replaces Electric Terrain.
answers.failsTo: Re-entry.

prepReasoning.A: It's a damage boost on visible Electric attackers. Answers are typing.

cores.name: Grassy Terrain (Rillaboom) core
cores.oneLineWhy: Rillaboom is the most-used mon in M-C (35%). Grassy Terrain powers priority Grassy Glide, heals and halves Earthquake. Grassy Seed adds Unburden or +1 Def.

detection.blindSpot: The meta's real partner trigger is the Grassy Seed item (Gholdengo, Sneasler). dex.json has no items, so seed partners aren't detected. pokemon.json usage.topItems would allow it.

answers.label: Resists Grass
answers.note: Blunts Grassy Glide / Wood Hammer.
answers.failsTo: U-turn / High Horsepower coverage.

answers.label: Own terrain setter
answers.note: Removes Grassy Glide priority and the seed triggers.
answers.failsTo: Re-entry.

answers.label: Strong Fire / Flying hitter
answers.note: Super-effective on Rillaboom.
answers.failsTo: Intimidate, Fake Out.

prepReasoning.A: Rillaboom does its job regardless of what you know.

cores.name: Fake Out + redirection shell
cores.oneLineWhy: Two support slots buy the partner free turns to set speed control, set up or Mega Evolve.

answers.label: Spread attacks
answers.note: Spread moves ignore redirection.
answers.failsTo: Wide Guard. Spread damage is 0.75x.

answers.label: Ghost: Fake Out-immune
answers.note: Normal-type Fake Out can't touch it.
answers.failsTo: Scrappy Fake Out (Kangaskhan).

answers.label: Inner Focus
answers.note: Can't flinch.
answers.failsTo: Takes the chip damage anyway.

answers.label: Grass: ignores Rage Powder
answers.note: Grass-types and Overcoat ignore Rage Powder (not Follow Me).
answers.failsTo: Follow Me users.

answers.label: Ignores redirection
answers.note: Single-target moves go where you aimed them.
answers.failsTo: Protect.

prepReasoning.A: Its value comes from turn order, not secrecy.

cores.name: Perish trap
cores.oneLineWhy: Perish Song plus trapping forces KOs through Protect, usually with Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag.

answers.label: Ghost: can't be trapped
answers.note: Ghost-types switch out of any trap.
answers.failsTo: Perish still counts down while it stays in.

answers.label: Pivot out
answers.note: Pivot moves escape trapping and reset the Perish count.
answers.failsTo: Protect on the target (U-turn fails). Parting Shot is Taunt-able.

answers.label: Taunt the singer
answers.note: Perish Song is a status move, so Taunt stops it.
answers.failsTo: Mental Herb, a faster singer.

answers.label: Soundproof / Run Away
answers.note: Soundproof is immune to Perish Song. Champions' Run Away escapes trapping.
answers.failsTo: Partners without it.

prepReasoning.A: The core relies on the opponent not having a way out. A week's notice lets you build your 6 with Ghosts, pivots or Taunt. You can't prep if you don't know it's in their 6, but Perish Song users are few and visible in the pool.
prepReasoning.B: Preview confirms Perish Song. Even stronger for the defender.

cores.name: Intimidate cycling
cores.oneLineWhy: Two Intimidate users plus pivoting keep physical attackers at -1, -2.

answers.label: Special attacker
answers.note: Intimidate doesn't touch Special Attack.
answers.failsTo: Snarl.

answers.label: Intimidate-proof ability
answers.note: Blocks the drop, or benefits from it.
answers.failsTo: Reliable against Intimidate itself. Doesn't help against other stat drops (Parting Shot, Snarl).

prepReasoning.A: The answer is roster structure, not tech.

cores.name: Screens + attackers
cores.oneLineWhy: Prankster Reflect / Light Screen cut damage to their side for 5 turns (8 with Light Clay) while attackers set up: about 0.67x (2732/4096) in doubles, 0.5x in singles (Showdown data/moves.ts reflect / lightscreen).

answers.label: Screen breaker
answers.note: Removes screens from their side.
answers.failsTo: Ghost-types (Brick Break). Protect.

answers.label: Infiltrator
answers.note: Ignores screens.
answers.failsTo: Nothing specific.

answers.label: Taunt the setter
answers.note: Stops screens if it lands first.
answers.failsTo: Prankster screens (+1) go first. Mental Herb.

prepReasoning.A: Screens are visible in the pool, and breakers (Brick Break, Psychic Fangs, Raging Bull) are a free move slot on many physical mons. A hidden breaker can catch them out.
prepReasoning.B: At preview the screens player sees your breaker or Infiltrator and can target it, delay screens or not bring the core. The defender's tech still deters, but it no longer surprises, so the core loses less to prep.

answerBlockers: answer.blockedBy lists conditions checked against EVERY mon in the opponent's drafted pool (any option). If any pool mon matches, the answer is 'contested': it still shows and counts as a candidate answer, but it can't be an anchor. In scenario A you can't know whether that protector is in their 6, so this is deliberately cautious. Items aren't seen (Mental Herb). Covert Cloak isn't in the M-C pool.
